findings.detail: The same renderer defect as Laws of Motion. Each of the 10 pre-attempt figures (5 in Core2A, 5 in Core2B) is emitted with every stage group, the later ones hidden only by CSS. Its aria-labelledby names a <desc> that narrates every stage, including the result. The accessible name of the Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-PROJECTILE-VALIDITY-04 pre-attempt image contains 'the projectile model starts at the release with the package's own velocity, u = (50, 0) m/s … −80 = −5t² gives t = 4 s, the package lands x = 50 × 4 = 200 m ahead'. That is the protected move and the answer. For Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2B-UNEQUAL-HEIGHT-03 it contains '(t − 0.5)(t − 1.5) = 0 … it lands at t = 1.5 s, 15 m out, with v = (10 i − 5 j) m/s'. A screen-reader learner hears these before attempting, and the page search matches them. A PRE_ATTEMPT mount must carry only the pre-attempt stage groups and a description of those stages alone.

Several representation <title>s state the protected move or the key answer. The title is shown on the pre-attempt figure as the SVG hover tooltip and the accessible name. 2B-04: 'Package released from a plane at 50 m/s, 80 m up: it starts with the plane's velocity' (the deciding move verbatim). 2B-02: '… crossing paths are not a collision unless both arrive at the same t' (the deciding move). 2B-03: '… two roots, chosen by x' (the deciding move). 2A-03: '… at the apex only v_y is zero' (answers hint rung 1 and the velocity part). 2A-05: '… landing where Δy = 0' (answers rung 1). Give these a situation-only title for the pre-attempt mount, e.g. 'A package released 80 m up from a plane flying level at 50 m/s'.

Each Core1B unit mounts its Core1A worked-anchor figure, pre-attempt and post-attempt, instead of a figure of its own attempt. The boat task (3 and 4 m/s, (15, 20) m at 5 s) shows the drone x = 6t, y = 8t − t². The skater (u = (5, 0) m/s, a = (−1, 2) m/s², 4 s) shows the puck with u = (4, 6), a = (0, −2). The basketball from 2 m (u = (6, 8) m/s, t = 0.5 s) shows the qualitative launched-versus-motor model gate. So the post-attempt reconstruction figure shows the Core1A answer, not this attempt's.

Two Core2A figures carry no values from their item. Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-SHARED-CLOCK-01 (x = 4t, y = 10 − 2t², position (8, 2) m at 2 s; the pair x(2 s), y(3 s) = (8, −8) m) mounts the generic SHARED-CLOCK figure, which draws qualitative velocity histories rather than the item's positions. Q-PHY-KIN-2D-2A-HORIZONTAL-LAUNCH-04 (15 m/s from 20 m; t = 2 s, 30 m, (15, −20) m/s) mounts EVENT-CLOCK, 'drawn qualitatively, without numerical values' (u_x, h, t_event). Both need an instance with the item's numbers, as the other three Core2A items now have.

Still open from the previous review. Core1 mounts the same SHARED-CLOCK figure (qualitative v_x and v_y histories) for all three microtopics. That includes MIC-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL, whose orientation needs the gravity-only gate (a_x = 0, a_y = −g), and MIC-PHY-KIN-2D-CONSTANT-ACCELERATION, whose compact anchor is u = (1, 2), a = (2, −2) → v = (5, −2) m/s at 2 s.

Still open. Every page's h1, <title> and breadcrumb read 'Owner-approved ExamSIDE question-demand slice for plane motion, now semantically': scope_summary cut mid-sentence, in internal provenance language. Use 'Motion in a plane' or the bucket title 'Two-dimensional kinematics and projectile model'.

The Core1B projectile reconstruct prompts ask 'What exact component condition identifies the event…', 'If the event is the apex, what becomes zero…' and 'Does launch height equal landing height?'. The attempt (basketball from 2 m, position and velocity at t = 0.5 s) has no named event, apex or landing. Replace them with prompts that rebuild this task: 'Where is the origin, so what is y at t = 0?', 'What is y(t) with the 2 m start?', 'At t = 0.5 s, is v_y still positive?'.

CU-PHY-KIN-PROJECTILE-MODEL-1 mounts the qualitative model-gate figure (object A in free flight, object B with its motor on). Its worked anchor, a ball from a balcony with u = (8, 6) m/s, displacement (8, 1) m and v = (8, −4) m/s at 1 s, is never drawn. The gate is correct physics, but the anchor has no figure.

The answer (A, B) is correct, but the working rejects (C) only by assertion ('For theta=30° the apex is not after P'). Add the calculation: at 30°, 1 = 5 tan 30° − 25g/(2v² cos² 30°) gives v² ≈ 8.83g; the slope at x = 5 m is tan 30° − 5g/(v² cos² 30°) ≈ 0.577 − 0.755 = −0.18 < 0, so the apex is before P and (C) is false.

Rung 4 does not climb past rung 3. Rung 3 already says 'use Δy = 0 to obtain the nonzero landing time', and rung 4 only adds 'the vertical equation has a launch root and a later root'. A climbing rung 4 would be: 'Factor 16t − 4t² = 4t(4 − t): which factor is the launch, and which is the landing?'.
